# Period start: the Monday date that identifies the payout week

> The Monday date that identifies which week the payout covers, stored as a DATEONLY field in the Payout table.

_Part of [Payout row with one-per-shop-per-week rule](payout-model.md)_

Every payout is for one shop in one week, and that week is identified by its Monday date. When the weekly payout job runs, it calculates the start of the current or target week (using the [Monday of the week, in UTC, as a date string](monday-of.md) helper), and uses that as `periodStart`. Combined with the shop ID, this creates a unique constraint: `UNIQUE(shopId, periodStart)`. If the job runs twice for the same week—because of a retry or duplicate message—it finds the existing payout instead of creating a second one, making the job safe to run idempotently. The field itself is just a date with no time component; Stripe and the ledger operations use it to group all the transfers and journals for that week.

**Look at:** [`periodStart` in payout.model.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/infra/models/payout.model.ts#L21)

## What it touches

| Kind | Name | How |
|---|---|---|
| database | `Payout.periodStart` | Stores the Monday date (DATEONLY) of the week for which this payout is calculated, keyed together with `shopId` to enforce one payout per shop per week. |

## Watch out

- DATEONLY has no time component, so the date is always midnight UTC—the time never varies.
- The unique constraint (`shopId`, `periodStart`) is what makes duplicate attempts find the existing payout; if you try to insert the same shop and week twice, the database silently skips or finds the first.
- Only Monday dates belong here; the calling code must use [`mondayOf`](weekly-seller-payouts.md) to calculate the start of the week, not any arbitrary date.
